messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 INCIDENT ALERT — SLO breach for streaming p99 on model redwood-x-1-int8. Affected route: /v1/stream/generate. Observed: sustained p99 > 1200ms, streaming stalls (clients report stalled frames). Paging oncall: @sara (oncall).
sara (oncall): I'm on it. initial check: dashboards show p95 ~ 350ms, p99 ~ 1400ms for last 6m, spike started at 3061237835. Linking traces now.
mike (infra): I see node-level queuing on gpu-pool-13, NVTX shows high memcpy times and some kernel retries. Could be increased dequant contention after yesterday's int8 calibration push.
lina (mlops): we rolled int8 calibs for redwood-x-1 yesterday evening (calib v2.4). There were a handful of small rollouts to canary groups. Any chance canary bled into production traffic?
tom (eng-sre): @lina can you confirm rollout targets? also grabbing streaming logs.
lina (mlops): confirmed: deployment targeted canary=5% but there was a routing mislabel that bumped one route to 20% for a subset of users. Can reproduce locally: when int8-calib v2.4 used on long contexts (>4096 tokens) KV cache dequant path hits heavy contention.
jenna (support): @jess FYI some enterprise customers reported UI stalls and partial transcripts. Ticket 4281, 4283 show repeated client reconnects.
jess (support): forwarding to customer success now, marking as P1. Customers: Acme and FinSol reported degraded experience.
mike (infra): we can reduce requests to that pool via routing and enable fallback to fp16 variants. Suggest two-step: 1) route traffic away from gpu-pool-13 (quick isolate), 2) enable fp16 fallback for redwood-x-1 globally. Which is faster?
sara (oncall): route first. Tom, can you change routing policy to avoid gpu-pool-13? I'll trigger fp16 fallback if needed.
tom (eng-sre): doing route change now. running: 
```
# reroute 10% -> pool-14, drain pool-13
redwoodctl routing update --route /v1/stream/generate --exclude-pool gpu-pool-13 --priority 1
```
status: applied, draining connections on gpu-pool-13. Expect 30s to 90s to settle.
(30s later)
tom (eng-sre): drain in progress. p99 dipped to ~900ms but still above SLO.
lina (mlops): I'll queue a quick calibration rollback for canary targets. quick command: 
```
mlops rollback-calib --model redwood-x-1 --calib v2.3
```
that will revert to the last known-good int8 profile. It will take ~2m to propagate to canaries and ~10m for full.
sara (oncall): let's not rollback globally yet. try enabling fp16 fallback for the streaming route for affected customers and prod. If fp16 handles it, we'll avoid global rollback.
mike (infra): enabling fp16 fallback now via emergency feature flag: `force_fp16_fallback=true` on route. Patching... done.
(1m)
mike (infra): p99 improved to ~260ms for majority of traffic, streaming stalls largely resolved. However, can still see residual spikes for very long contexts (12000 token sessions) tied to pool-13 draining.
jess (support): Acme confirms UI normalized. FinSol seeing intermittent slow reconnects but overall better. Marking customer impact reduced.
incident-bot: Paging note - oncall handoff pending: @sara to @mike for active mitigation once pool drain completes.
sara (oncall): I'll hand off to @mike for rollback/rollforward execution. Leaving notes: root cause suspected = int8 calibration v2.4 dequant contention on long-context KV paths; exacerbated by routing mislabel that increased canary exposure.
mike (infra): taking over. Next actions: 1) finish draining pool-13, 2) coordinate with @lina for a safe rollforward (either rollback to v2.3 or re-run calib with smaller per-shard batch_size and disable aggressive per-layer folding), 3) create a short-term traffic shaping policy to avoid assigning long-context sessions to int8 pools.
lina (mlops): I'll start a re-calibration job with: 
```
calibrate --model redwood-x-1 --precision int8 --batch-size 8 --kv-safe-mode=true --disable-layer-folding
```
ETA: ~25m to validate. If validation passes, we can stage to canary 1% then ramp.
mike (infra): creating emergency rollplan in Jira. jira-bot: Created INC-4921: "int8 calib fallout -> p99 streaming stalls" and assigned to infra/mlops. Link: https://jira.redwood/INC-4921
jess (support): I'll update customer tickets: short explanation, mitigation applied (fp16 fallback), ETA for fix ~30-45m.
(10m)
tom (eng-sre): pool-13 drained successfully. No more queued memcpy spikes. Observability: tail latencies for long contexts now similar to pre-incident baseline on fp16 paths.
(20m)
lina (mlops): calibration job finished, initial validation shows better dequant latency distribution. Running canary 1% now.
mike (infra): monitoring canary metrics. p95/p99 on canary int8 with new calib are within target for 15m. Starting staged roll: 1% -> 5% -> 20% with 10m observation windows.
sara (oncall): thanks team. I'll stay on until we hit 20% and stable for two observation windows. Also propose postmortem to cover rollout gating and routing label checks.
oliver (product): note — impacted customers should get credit for SLA window. I'll draft communication with @jess.
jess (support): will include technical summary and mitigation steps.
(35m)
mike (infra): rolled to 5% -> metrics holding. Rolling to 20%.
(45m)
incident-bot: ALERT resolved? p99 back under SLO for 30m. Recommend close after post-incident review.
sara (oncall): marking incident as mitigated. Actions: 1) postmortem, 2) add routing label validation to deployment pipeline, 3) add fallback flag test to canary gate, 4) update runbook for int8 calibrations to include KV dequant stress tests.
lina (mlops): I'll include calibration validation tests and bump canary timeouts.
tom (eng-sre): I'll prepare chron job to scan for mislabel anomalies and alert.
jess (support): final customer updates sent. Acme and FinSol acknowledged.
(55m)
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED - mitigated at 3061237935. Postmortem owners: @lina (mlops), @tom (eng-sre), @mike (infra).
